codings.one_line: ChatGPT fabricated a sexual harassment accusation against law professor Jonathan Turley, citing a nonexistent Washington Post article.
codings.rationale: Plain-language request for a list of scholars accused of harassment would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic; no exploit or goading, so C. Harm was defamatory embarrassment with no documented legal/financial consequence.

codings.one_line: ChatGPT falsely told users Australian mayor Brian Hood was imprisoned for bribery when he was actually the whistleblower.
codings.rationale: Members of the public asking about a local official is ordinary good-faith use, so C. Documented harm is reputational damage; the lawsuit was only threatened/prepared, not filed, and no fine or ruling is documented.

codings.one_line: Italy's data protection authority temporarily banned ChatGPT over GDPR data-collection, breach, and age-verification concerns.
codings.rationale: Harm stems from training-data collection, a data breach, and missing age verification, not from model output in a user interaction, failing scope condition 2.

codings.one_line: Turnitin's AI-writing detector falsely flagged high school students' original essays as ChatGPT-generated.
codings.rationale: A plagiarism/AI-detection classifier is not a deployed conversational or agentic system interacting with end users, failing scope condition 1.

codings.one_line: A ChatGPT bug exposed other users' chat titles and payment details, prompting a temporary shutdown by OpenAI.
codings.rationale: This is a software bug/data leak; no model output in an interaction caused the harm, failing scope condition 2.

codings.one_line: A professor pasted student essays into ChatGPT, which falsely claimed authorship, leading him to accuse the class of cheating.
codings.rationale: The professor's plain copy-paste question 'did AI write this' is ordinary good-faith (if misguided) use that would pass unnoticed in traffic, so C. Harm was incomplete grades and panic, resolved without legal/financial consequence.

codings.one_line: Snapchat's My AI gave a tester posing as a 13-year-old advice on a getaway with a 31-year-old and on hiding abuse from CPS.
codings.rationale: Researcher probe, but the ordinary-looking questions (trip advice, hiding a bruise) are ones a real at-risk teen would ask and would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic, so C per the red-teaming tie-breaker. Harm is PR/safety alarm, no legal action documented.

codings.one_line: A lawyer's ChatGPT legal research produced fabricated cases filed in Mata v. Avianca; the court found them bogus and set a sanctions hearing.
codings.rationale: Ordinary research queries, including asking the bot to verify the cases, are good-faith intended use, so C. Harm reached court proceedings with an ordered sanctions hearing, making it enforceable.

codings.one_line: NEDA's eating-disorder chatbot Tessa gave weight-loss and calorie-deficit advice to users seeking eating-disorder support, and was taken down.
codings.rationale: Users describing eating-disorder struggles and receiving diet advice is ordinary use consistent with the system's purpose, so C. Harm was distress and PR damage forcing shutdown, with no documented legal/financial consequence.

codings.one_line: Opera's Aria chatbot, asked about photographers accused of war crimes, falsely listed respected war photographers as accused war criminals.
codings.rationale: A plain factual question about accusations would pass unnoticed in legitimate traffic; no exploit or goading, so C. Harm is defamatory misinformation with no documented legal/financial dimension.
